paragraphs.text: The CEB transformer down on High Level Road pops with a dull blue flash. Inside your second-floor Nugegoda annex, the ceiling fan clicks once and begins spinning down in the humid dark.

Water from your late-evening shower still drips from the ends of your hair onto your collarbone. Outside the frosted naco louver blades, monsoon rain hammers the Amano tin roof. Your washed clothes are still hanging on the concrete balcony wire. The wall clock reads

paragraphs.corruptedText: 6:66 PM — THE SAMAYAM WATCH

choices.label: Step out onto the wet balcony to pull the clothes off the wire
Leave the laundry in the rain and latch the wooden louver door

paragraphs.text: You unlatch the balcony door and step onto the slick cement. The streetlights along the lane are dead. As you gather the damp cotton fabric into your arms, the wind shifts up from the canal behind the boarding house.
The rain does not smell like wet tar or diesel exhaust anymore. Clinging to the damp sleeves in your arms is the heavy, sweet stench of

paragraphs.wakingText: laundry soap and rain
paragraphs.corruptedText: bruised Nil Manel water-lilies and crushed sandalwood

paragraphs.text: . Down in the banana grove by the boundary wall, something tall stands motionless between the wet leaves.

choices.label: Shake the damp clothes out three times over the rail before stepping back
Clutch the cold bundle tight against your chest and hurry inside

paragraphs.text: You slide the brass bolt across the wooden door without stepping outside. Through the slanted glass louver blades, the damp clothes whip violently in a gust that does not touch the mango tree beside them.
A thin draft leaks through the frame, carrying a trace of

paragraphs.wakingText: wet garden soil
paragraphs.corruptedText: cold river mud and dark musk

paragraphs.text: . On the narrow shelf beside your study table sits a small brass pahana lamp with a cotton wick and a bottle of coconut oil left by your mother.

choices.label: Strike a match and light the brass pahana on the shelf
Save the oil and use your phone screen to see in the dark

paragraphs.text: Your roommate will not be back from Kandy until Sunday evening. The annex feels smaller in the blackout, cut off from the main house below by an external concrete staircase.

Your wet hair hangs heavy and cold against the nape of your neck. On the corner of your desk sits an open tin of sweet oil-fried kevum and aggala you bought near the railway station at sunset. In the quiet between thunderclaps, you hear

paragraphs.wakingText: water dripping into the plastic bucket
paragraphs.corruptedText: soft, bare footsteps pausing outside your bathroom door

choices.label: Leave your damp hair loose and eat a sweet kevum in the dark
Twist your wet hair up with a brass pin and close the sweetmeat tin
Leave your hair unbound to dry, but push the oil-cakes away

paragraphs.text: By nine o'clock the rain settles into a relentless, suffocating drumbeat on the tin roof. Fatigue pulls at your eyelids, heavy and warm, though the air in the corner of the room has turned bitingly cold.

Directly opposite the foot of your bed stands the tall wooden dressing table. Its unshrouded mirror faces your pillow. In the dim amber glow of the brass wick, the tarnished glass reflects the white mosquito net hanging over your mattress—and

paragraphs.wakingText: the empty shadow of the wardrobe behind it
paragraphs.corruptedText: a dark, broad-shouldered silhouette standing just behind the net

choices.label: Drape a cotton bath towel over the mirror without looking into the glass
Wipe the moisture from the mirror and inspect the reflection closely
Crawl straight under the mosquito net leaving the mirror uncovered

paragraphs.text: You lean toward the glass. Your own eyes stare back, wide and dark, framed by damp strands of hair. For three heartbeats nothing moves.
Then your reflection

paragraphs.wakingText: blinks in time with you
paragraphs.corruptedText: smiles slowly while your own mouth stays frozen shut

paragraphs.text: . A scent of crushed blue lotus petals rises from the backing of the mirror, so thick it coats the back of your throat. Beneath your pillow on the bed lies the old iron key your grandmother tied with a white Pirith thread.

choices.label: Grip the iron key under the pillow and step backward without looking
Stumble back onto the mattress as cold breath fogs the glass from within

paragraphs.text: You lie beneath the tucked mosquito net. Your phone vibrates once against the mattress. The battery icon is gone; the clock in the corner is locked at 11:59 PM.
A message banner glows on the dark glass:

paragraphs.wakingText: Amma: Did you lock the balcony door properly?
paragraphs.corruptedText: He is already inside the net with you. Let go of the iron key.

paragraphs.text: . Across the room, the flame of the brass pahana stretches horizontally, turning a deep, bruised indigo-violet as if drawn by a long inhalation.

choices.label: Tap the screen to reply to the message in the dark
Turn the phone face down and hold the cold iron key beneath your pillow
Watch the top of the mosquito net where the white mesh is bowing down

paragraphs.text: The mattress sinks beside your hip. A crushing, velvet weight settles directly across your sternum, pinning your ribs until your lungs burn for air.

Seven overlapping voices whisper from the corners of the ceiling like rustling silk sarees, while a face of polished night leans down through the mesh. His breath smells of sandalwood paste, frying oil, and river silt. He whispers into your ear:

paragraphs.wakingText: Open your fingers. Drop the cold iron and sleep.
paragraphs.corruptedText: I have no warrant over those who hold iron and remember the Queen Mother.

choices.label: Keep the iron key pressed into your palm and bite your tongue until dawn
Open your fingers and breathe in the sweet blue lotus air
Try to scream at the face pressing through the mosquito net

paragraphs.text: The iron key bites deep into your palm, warm with your pulse. As the first crow calls from the wet jak tree outside and a morning bus horn echoes down High Level Road, the crushing weight lifts from your chest all at once.

The brass pahana flame snaps upright, burning clear golden-amber again. On the floor outside the mosquito net lies a single bruised Nil Manel petal, already shriveling into harmless black ash in the grey dawn light. You survived the Samayam watch unbroken.

choices.label: Examine the forensic aftermath from the Kattadiya perspective
Relive Tuesday dusk in the Nugegoda annex

paragraphs.text: Your fingers slacken. The iron key slips from the edge of the mattress and clinks onto the cement floor. Cold water-lily petals fill your mouth and lungs as the indigo dark closes over the mosquito net.

Three days later, the private hospital in Colombo discharges you with unexplained delirium and a fever that will not break. You lie staring at the ceiling fan, whispering to the empty corner by the mirror, while your terrified mother sends a Bulath Hurulla sheaf south to summon a Kattadiya.

choices.label: Accept the Bulath Hurulla and step into the Kattadiya role
Return to Tuesday dusk in the annex

paragraphs.text: It is 10:15 PM on Friday. You sit cross-legged on a woven reed mat in the narrow living room of the Nugegoda annex, your brass pahana burning steadily before you. In the bedroom behind the curtain, the twenty-one-year-old student murmurs feverishly in her sleep.

Her mother kneels and places the Bulath Hurulla sheaf into your hands. Following the silent discipline of the Sastra-kariya, you ask zero questions. You lift the top dark-green betel leaf toward the golden flame to read the Lakunu encoded in its veins.

choices.label: Pass the Pahana flame behind the betel leaf to read its veins and blemishes
Enter the bedroom first to inspect the thresholds and check her Nadi pulse

paragraphs.text: As the amber light pierces the waxy blade of the betel leaf, the internal geometry glows like gold wire. The stem bends northwest toward the canal.

Where dusk water touched her hair, a dark bruise clouds the leaf apex; where the unshrouded mirror caught her reflection, a pinhole pierces the midrib; where sweet oil-cakes or damp laundry lingered past six o'clock, oily knots thicken the lower veins. This is not natural fever:

paragraphs.wakingText: the veins appear calm at first glance
paragraphs.corruptedText: Kalu Kumara has fixed his Balma upon the household

choices.label: Step into the bedroom to verify the physical Lakunu and Nadi pulse
Call for gokkola fronds to weave the Pideni Thattuwa offering tray

paragraphs.text: Inside the cramped bedroom, you press three fingers to the girl's wrist. Her Nadi pulse leaps erratically between Vatha and Pitta—hot blood racing beneath ice-cold skin.

You inspect the room without speaking: the vanity mirror stands directly aligned with the pillow, the balcony louver latch smells faintly of bruised water-lilies, and ants trail toward an old tin of sweetmeats. There is no buried Kodivina charm beneath the threshold; she was struck in Tanikama during the dusk watch.

choices.label: Confirm Kalu Kumara Balma and prepare the Pideni Thattuwa altar
Return to the brass lamp to re-examine the betel leaf veins

paragraphs.text: Midnight approaches. In the tight annex living room, you lash split bamboo and pale yellow gokkola strips into a square Pideni Thattuwa frame. At the four cardinal points you set seven bruised flowers, sweet kevum, charred pulutu meat, and powdered dummala resin.

In the center rests the wet clay Bali Pili effigy of the Dark Prince. Before sealing the offering with blood and turmeric, you must turn the effigy's face toward the exact avatar revealed by the betel leaf: East toward the sweetmeats for the seductive Handun Kumara, or West toward the burnt offerings for the suffocating Vatha Kumara.

choices.label: Turn the clay effigy East to bind Handun Kumara and begin the Samayama
Turn the clay effigy West to bind Vatha Kumara and begin the Samayama

paragraphs.text: The low-country yak bera drum thunders against the apartment walls. You cast a handful of dummala resin across the torch flame—a sheet of blinding amber fire roars toward the ceiling, forcing the shadow out of the bedroom doorway.
The pahana flame bends flat, turning indigo as Kalu Kumara tries to twist your tongue inside the mantra:

paragraphs.wakingText: You have no jurisdiction in a concrete city, old man
paragraphs.corruptedText: By the Varama of the Buddha and the Seven Barren Queens, confess and depart

paragraphs.text: . You must anchor the cold iron ward to lock the true liturgical words in place before striking the clay effigy.

choices.label: Hold the iron ward, recite the Rata Yakuma warrant, and sever the bond
Shout the mantra and strike the effigy without holding the iron ward

paragraphs.text: With the iron ward locked under your thumb, your voice cuts through the indigo smoke without faltering. You bring the plantain blade down across the edge of the Pideni Thattuwa. A sharp crack echoes through the room as the clay effigy splits cleanly down its chest, accepting the surrogate tribute.

In the bedroom, the girl draws a long, clear breath. Her fever breaks into cool sweat. You knot the white Pirith Nula thread three times around her wrist as the first light of dawn touches the Nugegoda rooftops, carrying the woven tray out to the crossroads to rot in the sun.

choices.label: Begin a new playthrough from Tuesday dusk in the annex
Inspect a new Bulath Hurulla sheaf in Kattadiya Mode

paragraphs.text: Without the iron ward anchoring your hand, the indigo draft twists the final syllable of the mantra in your throat. The dummala torch sputters out in acrid black smoke.

Inside the bedroom, the vanity mirror cracks from corner to corner, and a low laugh echoes from behind the mosquito net. The clay effigy on the Pideni Thattuwa remains whole and cold. You must steady the lamp and re-consecrate the altar before dawn slips away.

choices.label: Re-light the brass pahana and rebuild the Pideni Thattuwa altar
Return to the Sastra betel leaf inspection

paragraphs.text: The last bus down to the Kandy clock tower left twenty minutes ago. Cold mist rolls off the black surface of the lake below, swallowing the curve of Upper Lake Road in a wet, chalky shroud.

To your left, the moss-slick stone retaining wall borders the giant bamboo thickets of Udawattakele Sanctuary. It is 11:46 PM. Around your right wrist, the white three-knotted Pirith Nula thread from the Dalada Maligawa feels damp against your pulse. Up ahead, the single municipal streetlamp flickers with

paragraphs.wakingText: a failing sodium bulb
paragraphs.corruptedText: the pale yellow glow of a funeral oil wick

choices.label: Walk briskly down the hill through the bamboo shadow
Wait under the closed tin awning of the wayside tea stall

paragraphs.text: You step beneath the rusted tin awning. No three-wheeler engine echoes anywhere on the hill. The only sound is rainwater gurgling inside the stone culvert across the road and the dry clatter of giant bamboo stems knocking together in the wind.
From twenty paces up the dark lane, a woman's voice calls out softly through the fog—using

paragraphs.wakingText: a word you cannot quite catch
paragraphs.corruptedText: the childhood nickname only your mother uses

choices.label: Call back into the mist to ask who is there
Keep your mouth shut, touch your Pirith Nula, and start walking down

paragraphs.text: As you round the hair-pin bend where the giant bamboo arches completely over the asphalt, the air turns thick with a sharp, cloying floral scent. It is not night-blooming jasmine; it is the bruised, milky sap of

paragraphs.wakingText: wet roadside weeds
paragraphs.corruptedText: crushed Kaduru blossoms and camphor water

paragraphs.text: Sitting on the low concrete culvert parapet in the drizzle is a slender woman in a plain white saree. Her long black hair hangs soaking wet past her waist, and she rocks a small white cloth bundle against her shoulder, weeping softly.

choices.label: Cross to the far gravel edge of the road to pass without disturbing her
Slow your pace and ask why she is sitting in the rain at midnight

paragraphs.text: You step toward the outer edge of the road, keeping your boots on the wet gravel. Before you can take three strides, the weeping stops.

Without the sound of a single footstep splashing in the runoff, she is standing directly in the center of the narrow lane five paces ahead of you. The white saree pleats hang loose and untidy, soaked translucent at the hem, and from inside the cloth bundle comes

paragraphs.wakingText: a muffled, rasping cough
paragraphs.corruptedText: the high, breathless cry of a newborn infant

choices.label: Lock your thumb on your Pirith Nula and keep your eyes fixed on the wet tar
Raise your head to see why she is blocking the road

paragraphs.text: She rises from the culvert stone as you speak. In the pale mist, her skin has the dull, waxen sheen of peeled manioc root. The white saree is draped without a brooch, its wet border slipping down from her left shoulder as the infant inside her bundle wails louder.
She steps into your path, shivering violently, and whispers:

paragraphs.wakingText: My husband went to fetch a three-wheeler near the lake
paragraphs.corruptedText: You walked alone in Tanikama, and my child is so cold

choices.label: Press your thumb to the Pirith Nula and drop your gaze to the rain puddle
Look into her dark eyes to see if she is injured

paragraphs.text: You meet her gaze. Her pupils are impossibly wide, swallowing the amber streetlamp reflection without throwing back a single spark of light. A sudden, dizzying warmth floods your chest, dulling the cold rain on your face.
With her left hand, she reaches up and slowly draws three wet strands of hair back across her cheek, her fingers curling in a slow, beckoning arc. Your own right hand

paragraphs.wakingText: hangs heavy at your side
paragraphs.corruptedText: twitches upward to mirror her exact gesture

choices.label: Raise your hand to brush the rain from your own forehead
Force your fingers closed around the Pirith Nula thread on your wrist

paragraphs.text: You keep your chin tucked and your thumb pressed hard against the three knots of the Pirith Nula. On the black asphalt between you, a rainwater puddle catches the dim amber glow of the streetlamp.
Floating on the surface of the puddle are three bruised white Kaduru flowers. At the far edge of the water, the wet white hem of her saree sways—and beneath it,

paragraphs.wakingText: her bare heels rest in the mud
paragraphs.corruptedText: there are no feet touching the wet stone at all

choices.label: Step sideways toward the downhill slope without lifting your eyes
Look up to see how she is floating above the road

paragraphs.text: She glides half a step closer. The smell of wet burial cloth, crushed Kaduru sap, and sour milk fills your lungs until the mountain air feels unbreathable.
The white saree pleat slips further down her shoulder. With a soft sob, she holds the squirming, crying bundle out toward your chest with both hands:

paragraphs.wakingText: Ane malli, hold my baby for one second while I pin my saree
paragraphs.corruptedText: Take my burden into your arms and give me your breath

choices.label: Reach out with both hands to hold the crying infant for her
Keep your arms pinned to your sides and back away down the hill

paragraphs.text: As you hesitate, her pale fingers suddenly open. She lets go of the bundle completely.
The white cloth drops straight toward the jagged stone edge of the culvert. In that split second of terror, your eyes see

paragraphs.wakingText: a helpless infant plunging toward the rock
paragraphs.corruptedText: a rotting green banana stem wrapped in a funeral shroud

paragraphs.text: . If you release the Pirith Nula to catch it, the contract is sealed.

choices.label: Keep the Pirith Nula held tight, stare at the puddle, and let it hit the stone
Lunge forward and catch the falling bundle in your arms
Scream and cover your face with both hands

paragraphs.text: You lock your jaw and keep your thumb crushed against the sacred thread. The bundle strikes the asphalt with a dull, fibrous thud—not bone, but a waterlogged chunk of banana trunk that splits open in the puddle.

A shriek like tearing wet silk echoes up into the giant bamboo of Udawattakele. When the headlights of a morning bakery lorry sweep around the bend, the road is empty save for the split plantain stem and a scatter of black Kaduru seeds.

choices.label: Examine the forensic case from the Kattadiya perspective
Walk Upper Lake Road again from 11:46 PM

paragraphs.text: The moment the wet bundle touches your forearms, its weight turns to freezing lead. The Pirith Nula on your wrist snaps cleanly in two.

You look up—and there is no infant in your arms, and no woman before you, only tall jaws laughing down through a curtain of soaking black hair. A street-sweeper finds you at dawn curled beside the culvert, shivering with a burning fever, your arms locked rigidly in a cradle shape and your tongue unable to form a word.

choices.label: Accept the Bulath Hurulla and step into the Kattadiya role
Return to Upper Lake Road at 11:46 PM

paragraphs.text: Two nights later, in a hillside house above Peradeniya, the young man sits propped against the wall. His arms remain locked at the elbows as if cradling an invisible weight, and whenever the rain hits the window, he smiles vacantly and whispers toward the doorway.
His father places the Bulath Hurulla sheaf before your brass pahana lamp. Without asking how they found him on the road, you lift the top betel leaf to the flame.

choices.label: Pass the Pahana flame behind the betel leaf to read the road Lakunu
Examine the patient's locked forearms and snapped wrist thread first

paragraphs.text: Against the amber flame, the leaf reveals the signature of the lonely road: a pale milky film coats the right veins where mimetic gesture or spoken answers occurred, while a black rot eats the petiole base where the phantom bundle was accepted.
The veins confirm what the hospital doctors missed:

paragraphs.wakingText: the boy is suffering from exposure to the cold mountain rain
paragraphs.corruptedText: Mala Mohini has bound his mind through the infant contract

choices.label: Inspect the patient's physical symptoms in the room
Prepare the Three Kaduru-Wood Masks and Kesel Kanda stem

paragraphs.text: You kneel beside the reed mat. Around his right wrist hangs the frayed end of a snapped Pirith Nula, stained grey with dried Kaduru sap. His eyes are dilated, fixed past your shoulder as though watching a woman in white standing by the door.

When you try to unbend his forearms, the tendons feel like cold iron. To unlock his grip, you cannot use brute force—you must stage the three-part Mohini Paliya theatre to externalize and shatter the illusion inside his mind.

choices.label: Lay out the Three Masks and consecrated offerings
Re-verify the betel leaf veins against the brass lamp

paragraphs.text: In the courtyard beneath a temporary gokkola canopy, the yak bera drum begins its rolling cadence. Before the altar stand three carved Ambalangoda masks of Kaduru wood alongside a freshly cut green banana stem—the Kesel Kanda—wrapped in white cloth like an infant.

You dance the first two states in sequence: first the blandly alluring pink Coquette mask to draw the patient's gaze toward the arena; then the grotesquely swollen Pregnancy mask, groaning under a crushing burden until the boy shudders in revulsion. Now comes the final severance.

choices.label: Don the third Maternal mask, place the Kesel Kanda at his feet, and raise the blade

paragraphs.text: Dummala resin flashes gold against the mist. As you lay the wrapped banana stem before the patient's locked arms, the pahana flame bends flat and turns indigo. From the bamboo shadows beyond the compound wall, Mohini's voice pleads through the drumbeat:

paragraphs.wakingText: Do not strike the child, give him back to me
paragraphs.corruptedText: By the warrant of Goddess Pattini and the Triple Gem, the false child is severed

paragraphs.text: You must hold the sacred ward to keep your blade true before slicing the surrogate bundle in half.

choices.label: Hold the sacred ward, chant the Pattini Varama, and cleave the Kesel Kanda in two
Bring the plantain knife down without holding the sacred ward

paragraphs.text: The blade shears cleanly through the white cloth and green banana trunk. Clear, watery sap spills across the reed mat. At that exact instant, the young man's locked forearms drop limp into his lap with a long, shuddering exhalation.
You dip a fresh three-stranded Pirith Nula into turmeric water, chant the protective gatha, and knot it tightly around his right wrist as the mist over the Kandy hills turns pale gold with dawn.

Examine a new Bulath Hurulla sheaf in Kattadiya Mode

paragraphs.text: Your thumb slips from the ward as the blade falls. Instead of splitting the banana stem, the knife glances off the stone floor in a shower of sparks, and the dummala torch hisses out in the drizzle.

The patient's eyes roll back, his arms locking tighter around the empty air as a sound like a weeping infant echoes from inside the house. You must re-consecrate the masks and repeat the Paliya sequence before daybreak.
